newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-S.African reserves seen under 10 bln rand.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-S.African reserves seen under 10 bln rand.

text.p: South Africa's meagre gold and foreign exchange reserves are expected to have been drained further in October, a casualty of the ailing rand, economists said on Friday.
But the Reserve Bank's intervention in the foreign exchange market was likely to have been offset by government's offshore borrowings in September and October, they said.
The eleven economists polled by Reuters forecast gross reserves would decline to 9.6 billion rand from 10 billion rand in September, equivalent to just under four weeks import cover.
The consensus was drawn from a range of 9.0 to 10.5 billion rand with most economists predicting a flat to slightly lower number.

Economists estimate that the rand's descent to a record low of 4.7670 bid towards the end of the month cost the Reserve Bank between 500 million and one billion rand in reserves as it tried to defend the beleaguered currency.
"The Bank probably lost reserves trying to prop up the rand in the latter part of the month," said economist Peter Perkins of mining house JCI Ltd.
Further pressure was likely to have been brought to bear by the net foreign sales of local gilts and equities which amounted to just under 1.5 billion rand in the calendar month, economists said.
However, ING Barings economist Hania Farhan said that while she expected reserves to have declined, the fall would be balanced by the proceeds of South Africa's foreign bond issues.
The country raised 500 million Deutschmark in the Eurobond market in September and launched a $300 million Yankee bond in October.

Perkins noted that while the proceeds of both issues came through during October, the bulk of the Deutschmark issue was used to repay a DM400 million issue launched in 1991 which matured on October 10.
The capital repayment coupled with interest and cost expenses were expected to have resulted in about DM50 million flowing into the country.
An unknown factor in the equation would be whether which the central bank drew down on its foreign credit lines.

Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals told Reuters on Monday that the central Bank had not used any lines by Monday and economists assumed that the bank had not done so in the last four days of the month.
Indications were that the 612 million rand it drew down in September had been repaid, economists said.
One economist, who asked not to be identified, predicted an increase in the number, differing with economists on net foreign gilt sales because of settlement dates.

The economist used net foreign gilt purchases between mid-September and mid-October of about 600 million rand and also included some of the proceeds of loans by telecommunications utility Telkom and transport parastatal Transnet which amounted to about $150 million each.
"I am going for an increase of about 400 million rand," the economist said.
The data will be released next Thursday at 1600 GMT.
Also due for release next week is September producer inflation data.
Economists forecast a consensus 0.9 percent month-on-month rise and a 8.2 percent year-on-year rise compared with August's 1.0 and 7.4 percent increase.
The average was drawn from a range of 8.0 to 8.5 percent.
Economists said the imported component and food prices were expected to contribute the bulk of the monthly increase.

Rand Merchant Bank Treasury economist Julia Roy said that a low base effect would also be an important factor in the latest data. PPI rose just 0.1 percent month-on-month in September 1995, while the imported component fell by 0.1 percent over the same period.

SMK Securities economist Herman van Papendorp also noted that there has been concern that the other minerals category in the index, which has 4.33 percent weighting in the overall index and mainly consists of crude oil, could rise sharply.
Economists have questioned the fact that the category has been steady and even declined in recent months despite sharp increases in rand crude oil prices.
The figures will be released on Tuesday at 0900 GMT.
